$schema_comment: TinyBolus formulary. Edit values here to correct doses/ranges; the app picks up changes on next launch (via remote fetch). Item types: 'linear' (factor * weight), 'linear_range' (low..high * weight), 'linear_max' (factor * weight, capped at max), 'fixed' (string value, no calc), 'computed' (dispatches to a named calculator in lib/calculators/). All weights in kg. Units: mg, µg (microgram), mL, mL/h, J, cm.
$references_comment: Normalized citation map. Items reference entries here by key (see item.references: [...]). The About screen resolves each key to the full citation text. Keys are short but readable; pattern: first-author-or-body_topic_year.

items.name: Compression depth
items.note: not exceeding 6 cm at any age

items.name: C:V ratio
items.note: 15:2 if PBLS-trained · 30:2 untrained

items.name: Defibrillation
items.note: stepwise to 8 J/kg for refractory VF / pulseless VT (6th shock on) · adolescent 120–200 J

items.name: Cardioversion (synchronised)
items.note: double per attempt to max 4 J/kg

items.name: Adrenaline (cardiac arrest)
items.note: repeat every 3–5 min · max 1 mg/dose

items.name: Amiodarone
items.note: after 3rd shock · repeat after 5th · max 150 mg subsequent

items.name: Adrenaline (bradycardia)
items.note: unresponsive to oxygenation/ventilation · atropine if vagal

items.name: Adenosine (2nd dose)
items.note: escalate 0.05–0.1 mg/kg steps to max 0.5 mg/kg

items.name: Tidal Volume
items.note: per IDEAL body weight — if obese use estimated weight · lower end for neonates

items.name: Propofol
items.note: ≈ halve after sevoflurane induction

items.name: Ketamine (IM)
items.note: when IV access impractical · onset 3–5 min

items.name: Rocuronium
items.note: upper range for RSI

items.name: Succinylcholine (RSI)

brackets.note: raised in infants — larger extracellular volume

items.note: intubating dose · avoid in MH / hyperkalaemia risk

brackets.note: neonate: reduce · inject slowly (rigidity) · watch apnoea
<6 mo: prolonged effect · slow injection · hypotension with opioids

items.name: Midazolam (buccal premed)
items.note: if oral refused · seizures: see Emergency

items.name: Midazolam (IN premed)
items.note: 5 mg/mL — divide between nostrils

items.name: Dexamethasone (anti-inflammatory)
items.note: airway oedema / post-extubation stridor

items.name: Etomidate
items.note: for haemodynamic stability

items.name: Dexmedetomidine (IN premed)
items.note: 100 µg/mL solution · onset ~30 min

items.name: Thiopental
items.note: then 1 mg/kg PRN · titrate to effect

items.name: Paracetamol
items.note: interval ≥4 h

brackets.note: neonate: reduce · slow injection · watch apnoea

items.name: Ibuprofen (IV)
items.note: not <5 kg · infuse ≥10 min · PDA use is separate

items.name: Ibuprofen (oral)
items.note: not <5 kg

items.name: Tramadol
items.note: q6h · respiratory depression caution

items.name: Paracetamol (oral)
items.note: q4–6h

items.name: Adrenaline (cardiac arrest)
items.note: repeat every 3–5 min · max 1 mg/dose

items.name: Adrenaline (anaphylaxis IM)
items.note: repeat every 5 min PRN · pens: 150 µg 1–5 y · 300 µg 6–12 y · 500 µg >12 y

items.name: Adrenaline (anaphylaxis IV)
items.note: titrate to response · IM adrenaline is first-line

items.name: Ephedrine

brackets.note: ~10× older-child dose — indirect agent, immature sympathetics

items.note: ampoule 30 mg/mL — dilute

items.name: Phenylephrine
items.note: upper range for tet spells · hypotension: start low, titrate

items.name: Lidocaine
items.note: antiarrhythmic — refractory VF / pulseless VT

items.name: Glucose 10%
items.note: hypoglycaemia · recheck glucose after

items.name: Calcium gluconate 10%
items.note: hypocalcaemia · hyperkalaemia (ECG changes; not in arrest) · CCB overdose · slow IV

items.name: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4%
items.note: 1 mL/kg of 8.4% · TCA toxicity / severe acidosis · NOT for hyperkalaemic arrest

items.name: Dantrolene
items.note: reconstitute vials in 60 mL water NOW · repeat 1 mg/kg every 5 min · may exceed 10 mg/kg

items.name: Midazolam (buccal, status epilepticus)
items.note: seizure ≥5 min · 3–6 mo: hospital only · repeat once after 5–10 min

items.name: Midazolam (IV, status epilepticus)
items.note: use if IV/IO already in place — else buccal · repeat once · off-label use

items.name: Hydrocortisone (adrenal crisis)
items.note: then 1 mg/kg (max 50) q6h · saline 10 mL/kg bolus · glucose if low

items.name: Insulin + glucose (hyperkalaemia)
items.note: WITH glucose 10% 5 mL/kg — never insulin alone · check glucose & K+ q15min

items.name: Salbutamol (nebulized, hyperkalaemia)
items.note: 2.5 mg ≤25 kg · 5 mg >25 kg · repeat ≤5× · with insulin–glucose

items.name: Fluid Bolus
items.note: balanced crystalloid · cardiogenic: 5 mL/kg · adolescent max 500 mL

items.name: Maintenance
items.note: 4-2-1 (Holliday-Segar) · isotonic + glucose ± K+ · <1 mo: neonatal regimen

items.name: Tranexamic Acid
items.note: loading dose over 10 min · then 2 mg/kg/h infusion

items.name: Max allowable blood loss
items.note: estimate, not a transfusion trigger · EBV ~70–100 mL/kg

items.name: ETT
items.note: cuffed sizes — uncuffed add 0.5 (≥1 y) · neonatal table: uncuffed sizes

items.name: ETT insertion depth
items.note: nasal: +1 cm <1 y · +2–3 cm ≥1 y

items.name: Laryngoscope blade
items.note: Miller lifts the epiglottis · Macintosh 1 equally effective

items.name: Face mask
items.note: cover nose to chin cleft — anatomical fit over size

items.name: NG/OG tube
items.note: larger sizes for adolescent decompression

items.name: OPA / NPA sizing
items.note: OPA: incisors → angle of mandible · NPA: nostril → tragus; not in basal-skull fracture

items.name: Salbutamol (inhaled)
items.note: 100 µg/puff · repeat incrementally as needed

items.name: Salbutamol (nebulized)
items.note: repeat back-to-back or continuously per response

items.name: Magnesium Sulphate
items.note: severe asthma · infuse over 20 min

items.name: Clemastine
items.note: second-line, after adrenaline

items.name: Adrenaline (nebulized)
items.note: croup / stridor · 1:1000 (1 mg/mL)

items.name: Propofol (laryngospasm)
items.note: give in increments

items.name: Succinylcholine (laryngospasm)
items.note: 0.1 mg/kg may spare ventilation · avoid in MH / hyperkalaemia risk

items.name: Succinylcholine (IM)
items.note: laryngospasm / RSI without IV access · avoid in MH / hyperkalaemia risk

items.name: Rocuronium (laryngospasm)
items.note: when succinylcholine contraindicated (MH) — then secure airway · sugammadex 16 mg/kg

items.name: Salbutamol (IV, severe asthma)
items.note: bolus over 10 min · infusion 1–2 µg/kg/min (>2: PICU) · monitor K+ · off-label <12 y

items.name: Prednisolone (PO, asthma)
items.note: within the first hour · oral = IV efficacy · course ≤3 d, no taper

items.name: Hydrocortisone (IV, asthma)

weight_estimation.comment: APLS-updated. <1 month requires user input. >12 years requires user input.

ett_rules.comment: Neonatal weight-based UNCUFFED sizes per ERC 2025 Newborn Table 7 (v0.0.60 reband: ≤1.5 kg 2.5 / ≤3 kg 3.0 / ≤4 kg 3.5 – the previous ≤2 kg 3.0 / >2 kg 3.5 ran one size large at 2–3 kg), then infant age table (CUFFED, v0.0.43 Duracher/Motoyama), then CUFFED formula 3.5 + age/4 (uncuffed adds 0.5, ≥1 y only – see item note). Round formula result both ways to nearest 0.5. infant_under_1y_size kept as legacy fallback for pre-v0.0.43 binaries.

lma_table_comment: Bands overlap intentionally per v1 formularium. A patient in an overlap region shows both sizes; a patient in a single band additionally shows the next size up. min/max are INCLUSIVE on both ends.
auragain_table_comment: Ambu AuraGain sizing per IFU V7 (August 2023). Bands only overlap at boundary weights (5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 70, 100 kg) because min/max are INCLUSIVE on both ends, matching the lma_table convention so computeLma renders both tables consistently.

compression_depth.comment: Age-piecewise. Applies to the PALS section.
